guide.summary: Internal use, your own Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none); Agent serving many customers' Zendesk accounts (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal use, your own Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Agent serving many customers' Zendesk accounts (app review).

composio.note: Composio offers a managed Zendesk OAuth app, good for prototypes. For launch, create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: For a prototype, no: the Composio-managed app works. For production across customers, yes. Zendesk rules require your own approved global OAuth client, and managed apps show a Composio consent screen.
reasons: Zendesk requires multi-customer apps to use a global OAuth client issued to you
Managed app consent screen says Composio, not your brand
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Composio's default scopes may not cover your needs

prerequisites.title: Zendesk developer (d3v-) account
prerequisites.detail: Global client requests from accounts without the d3v- prefix are not accepted.

prerequisites.title: Registered Marketplace organization
prerequisites.detail: Register your organization at apps.zendesk.com so Zendesk knows who submits the app.

prerequisites.title: Zendesk Support or Chat accounts
prerequisites.detail: The global client covers Zendesk Support and Chat (Agent Workspace enabled) only. Sunshine Conversations bots need a separate token.

steps.title: Create Composio managed auth for prototype
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Zendesk app to prototype the agent flow before building your own app.

steps.title: Create OAuth client in Admin Center
steps.detail: In Admin Center go to Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients and add a client. Paste the Composio redirect URI, request only needed scopes, and save the secret immediately.
steps.done_when: You have the client identifier and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio custom auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret, then test the connection and scopes.
steps.done_when: A test account connects and tokens refresh.

steps.title: Draft scope list and global client request
steps.detail: List the exact API endpoints used, choose the narrowest scopes, and fill every field of the local client, including optional ones. Pick a zdg- identifier that is exactly the production value.
steps.done_when: The request form text is ready.

steps.title: Save client secret and identifier
steps.detail: Record both before requesting conversion, because you lose access to the client admin page afterwards.

steps.title: Submit global client request
steps.detail: In the Marketplace portal choose Global OAuth, click Request new OAuth, and submit it once the app is finished.

steps.title: Prepare and submit Marketplace app
steps.detail: Upload the ZIP, answer the compliance question accurately, then submit. Zendesk checks ZIP contents automatically.

steps.title: Wait for Zendesk approval
steps.detail: New submissions take 1-3 weeks. The global client approval time is not documented.

steps.title: Swap in global client credentials
steps.detail: Update the Composio auth config with the approved global client and check that refresh tokens work.
steps.done_when: Customers connect with the global client.

traps.title: Access token lifetime requested at token exchange must be
traps.detail: Access token lifetime requested at token exchange must be between 300 seconds (5 minutes) and 172,800 seconds (2 days).

traps.title: Refresh token lifetime requested must be between 604,800 seconds
traps.detail: Refresh token lifetime requested must be between 604,800 seconds (7 days) and 7,776,000 seconds (90 days).

traps.title: Customers cannot give you their own credentials
traps.detail: No third-party app may use a customer's API token or own OAuth client, listed or not. A multi-customer agent therefore needs the global client.

traps.title: Conversion removes client admin access
traps.detail: After your local client becomes global you lose its administration page. Save the secret and identifier first.

traps.title: Scopes outside the allowed set fail
traps.detail: Zendesk may restrict the global client to the scopes you listed. A request outside them returns 400 invalid_scope and no token. An empty scope request means full read and write.

traps.title: Short token lifetimes
traps.detail: New clients default to 30-minute access tokens and 30-day refresh tokens. An expired refresh token forces the user through full authorization again. Authorization codes last 120 seconds.

traps.title: Refresh token flow is mandatory
traps.detail: Global clients must support refresh tokens (required since January 31, 2026). Existing local clients must adopt it by April 1, 2027.

traps.title: Moving existing customers to OAuth
traps.detail: A hard cutover forces all customers to re-authorize at the same time.

traps.title: Customer data rules
traps.detail: Zendesk Developer Terms limit how you may use customer data.

blockers.what_it_means: You requested a scope outside the client's allowed scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only allowed scopes, or contact Zendesk Support to update them.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes with the approved list and fix the auth config.

blockers.what_it_means: Requests from accounts without the d3v- prefix are not accepted.
blockers.what_to_do: Request from a d3v- developer account.

blockers.what_it_means: The ZIP failed checks or the review found problems.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix the issues and resubmit with Submit Update on the original submission.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the ZIP against branding and compliance guidance.

open_questions: How long does Zendesk take to approve a global OAuth client request? Ask Zendesk Support or the Marketplace team.
Can the Composio-managed Zendesk app serve real customers in production? Ask Composio support.
Does Zendesk accept Composio's callback as the global client's redirect URI? Check with Zendesk when submitting the request.
Which Zendesk plans can create OAuth clients? Check the plan list in Zendesk's OAuth help article.

claims.text: Zendesk does not let developers create their own global OAuth clients; they must request one from Zendesk.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: On approval, Zendesk may set allowed scopes on the global client to limit it to the scopes the app needs.

claims.quote: When Zendesk approves your global OAuth client, Zendesk may configure allowed scopes on the client to restrict it to the scopes your app needs.

claims.text: Developers must register their organization before submitting Marketplace apps, so Zendesk knows who they are.

claims.text: Zendesk gives a turnaround of 1-3 weeks for new app submissions and 1-2 weeks for updates to existing apps.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: You can expect a turnaround time of 1-3 weeks for new app submissions and 1-2 week for updates to existing apps.

claims.text: The Marketplace review is described as checking that apps follow security best practices, including strong authentication, secure development, and data protection.

claims.text: The client identifier must be the exact value intended for production.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: A profile is optional and is only published once your app or theme has been approved and published on the Zendesk Marketplace.
evidence.answer: For the Zendesk Marketplace developer profile (not an OAuth app itself), the profile is optional and is not a precondition for customers to connect.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All Zendesk Marketplace profiles are reviewed by Zendesk.
evidence.answer: Zendesk reviews every Zendesk Marketplace profile, which is a marketplace listing review step and not a review of an OAuth app's scopes or connection rights.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If you’re submitting an app or theme for the first time, we’ll review your profile in conjunction with your app or theme.
evidence.answer: For a developer's first app or theme submission, Zendesk reviews the profile together with that app or theme.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Registering your organization and users is important so we know who you are when you submit apps or themes for review.
evidence.answer: For Zendesk Marketplace apps or themes, the developer must register its organization before submitting for review, so Zendesk knows who the developer is.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Complete your organization profile and click Submit .
evidence.answer: Organization registration on the Zendesk developer portal is completed by signing in at apps.zendesk.com, completing the organization profile, and clicking Submit.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All apps and integrations built for distribution to multiple Zendesk customers must be submitted to the Zendesk Marketplace for review and approval.
evidence.answer: Apps and integrations built for distribution to multiple Zendesk customers must be submitted to the Zendesk Marketplace for review and approval.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: This does not apply to private apps built by customers for their own internal use.
evidence.answer: The Marketplace submission requirement does not apply to private apps that customers build for their own internal use, so those can be used without Marketplace review.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If you haven’t listed your integration on the Zendesk Marketplace, you need to create your Zendesk Marketplace profile
evidence.answer: A developer whose integration is not on the Marketplace must create a Marketplace profile, register their organization, and submit the app for review and approval.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Ensuring that all Marketplace applications, integrations and bots follow security best practices—including strong authentication, secure development, and data protection—and undergo formal review by Zendesk is key to maintaining that trust.
evidence.answer: The Marketplace review is described as checking that apps follow security best practices, including strong authentication, secure development, and data protection.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Once the change is completed, you will need to submit an update to your existing listing in the Marketplace.
evidence.answer: After a change to an existing app to adopt the new standards, the developer must submit an update to its existing Marketplace listing, which means the listing is reviewed again.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Your customers will all be impacted at the same time and will be required to re-authorize their app or integration.
evidence.answer: When switching to OAuth in a hard cutover, customers will all be impacted at the same time and must re-authorize the app or integration.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Zendesk will be releasing a new page in Admin Center where customers can view and manage integrations that are using global OAuth access tokens.
evidence.answer: Zendesk is releasing a new Admin Center page where customers can view and manage integrations that use global OAuth access tokens.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If your public ZAF app needs to make server side calls to the Zendesk APIs, it’s required to use a global OAuth client and include custom headers
evidence.answer: Public ZAF apps that make server-side calls to the Zendesk APIs must use a global OAuth client and include custom headers.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Integration apps (also known as Marketing-only apps) are required to use a global OAuth client and each API call must include custom headers that specify the name of the integration, the organization ID, and the Marketplace app ID.
evidence.answer: Integration apps (also called Marketing-only apps) must use a global OAuth client, and each API call must include custom headers naming the integration, the organization ID, and the Marketplace app ID.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Supporting the refresh token flow will be required for all global OAuth clients starting January 31, 2026
evidence.answer: Supporting the refresh token flow will be required for all global OAuth clients starting January 31, 2026.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If you currently use API tokens or basic authentication with your integration to authenticate with Zendesk APIs, you will need to update your authentication method to use OAuth
evidence.answer: Apps currently using API tokens or basic authentication with Zendesk APIs must switch their authentication method to OAuth.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: It is not permissible for any third-party app, integration or bot (whether it’s listed on the Zendesk Marketplace or not) to use a customer’s API credentials (API token or a customer’s own OAuth client) to authenticate API calls.
evidence.answer: No third-party app, integration, or bot may use a customer's API credentials (an API token or a customer's own OAuth client) to authenticate API calls, whether or not it is listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.quote: You’re required to conform to rules about handling customer data, ensuring it is not misused or exposed to undue risk.
evidence.answer: Developers must follow rules on handling customer data so it is not misused or exposed to undue risk.

evidence.question: G11

evidence.answer: New limitations apply to how developers can use customer data, as set out in the Zendesk Developer Terms.

evidence.quote: Before submitting your app, make sure you have registered your organization on the Marketplace developer portal at apps.zendesk.com , and you're signed in to the portal.
evidence.answer: Before submitting a Zendesk Marketplace app, the developer's organization must be registered on the Marketplace developer portal and the developer must be signed in. This page covers Zendesk Marketplace app submission, not third-party OAuth apps.

evidence.answer: The ZIP file contents are also checked for compliance with Zendesk's Branding guidelines.

evidence.quote: Client kind - Public or Confidential.
evidence.answer: Client kind is set to Public or Confidential when creating the client.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Redirect URLs - Enter the URL or URLs that Zendesk should use to send the
evidence.answer: Redirect URLs are entered in the client form as the URLs Zendesk should send the user's decision to.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Scopes - Select the scopes this client can request.
evidence.answer: Scopes are selected in the client form.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Copy the Secret value to your clipboard and save it somewhere safe.
evidence.answer: After saving, a Secret field appears and its value should be copied and stored safely; it is the client_secret.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: For security reasons, your secret is displayed fully
evidence.answer: The secret is displayed fully only once, so the admin must save it when first shown.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Use the unique identifier and the secret value in your application as described in this
evidence.answer: The unique identifier and secret are used in the application when requesting tokens.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_id - Use the unique identifier specified in an OAuth client in the
evidence.answer: The client_id for token requests is the unique identifier from the OAuth client in Admin Center.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If you use the PKCE code_challenge and
evidence.answer: The client_secret is not required when the PKCE code_challenge and code_verifier parameters are used.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: These clients are required to use PKCE.
evidence.answer: Public OAuth clients (mobile and web apps) are required to use PKCE.

items.reason: The quote states the Marketplace submission requirement does not apply to private apps built for customers' own internal use.
The quote states the global-token requirement does not apply to internal-use applications or integrations.
The quote confirms OAuth clients are created and managed in Admin Center, but says nothing about the absence of a provider review step.
The quote states multi-customer apps must be submitted to the Marketplace for review and approval.
The quote states distributing a public or integration app to multiple customers requires global OAuth tokens.
The quote states regular API and OAuth tokens may not be used, because customers may not share their credentials with developers.
The quote states no third-party app, integration or bot may use a customer's API credentials, whether or not it is listed on the Marketplace.
The quote states that if the request is approved, Zendesk converts the local OAuth client to a global one.
The quote states Zendesk may configure allowed scopes on the global client when approving it.
The quote says registering is important so Zendesk knows who developers are on submission, but does not state it is a mandatory prerequisite.
The quote gives a 1-3 week turnaround for new submissions and 1-2 weeks for updates.
The quote describes the review as ensuring security best practices, including strong authentication, secure development and data protection.
The quote confirms the ZIP contents are checked automatically on upload, but does not say errors block submission.
The quote requires an accurate response to the compliance question, but says nothing about all mandatory questions needing answers.
The quote states that even fields labeled optional are required for global clients.
The quote states an out-of-scope request fails with 400 Bad Request and invalid_scope, with no token issued.
The quote states that if no scope is specified, the token defaults to full read and write access across all resources.
The quote says refresh tokens expire, but does not say that re-running the full authorization flow is then required.
The quote states the authorization code is valid for only 120 seconds.
The quote states that after the change, the developer must submit an update to the existing Marketplace listing.
The quote states that scope changes after approval go through Zendesk Support to update the allowed scopes.
The quote states customers will all be impacted at the same time and must re-authorize.
The quote states an account owner authorizes the service for their own subdomain.
The quote states Zendesk will release an Admin Center page for viewing and managing integrations using global OAuth tokens.
The quote states the instructions apply only to Support and Chat (Agent Workspace enabled) accounts, which excludes Sell.
The quote says the Support global OAuth cannot be used to build a Sunshine Conversations bot, but does not mention requesting a separate token.
The quote lists toggling Paid Apps, selecting a billing type and entering a Stripe Plan id.
The quote states new limitations on customer data use are introduced under the Developer Terms.
The quote states the preview app is not published or discoverable in the Marketplace and is instead sent by link to select customers.
The quotes state the Marketplace submission does not apply to customers' internal-use private apps and that the client is created in Admin Center, so no provider review is indicated.
The quotes support the single step of creating the OAuth client in Admin Center, with no provider step listed.
The quote states OAuth clients are created in Admin Center, which is the admin interface.
The quotes state multi-customer apps must be submitted to the Marketplace for review and approval, and Zendesk approves the global client.
The quotes state review and approval are required for apps distributed to multiple Zendesk customers, which is this setup's scenario.
The quotes cover submission, the local-to-global conversion and a registration note, but do not confirm the full ordered sequence or the 'publishes' step.
The quotes support the security check and a registration note on who you are, but nothing about checking why you need the data.
The quote gives 1-3 weeks for new Marketplace submissions; the statement that global client approval time is unknown is not addressed.
The quote states submissions from non-d3v- accounts are not accepted, which implies global client requests are limited to d3v- accounts.
The quote states no third-party app may use a customer's API token or own OAuth client to authenticate API calls.
The quotes say updates must be submitted to the listing and scope changes go through Support, but do not state that updates are approved again by Zendesk.
The quote states the account owner authorizes the service for their subdomain.
The quotes support the 1-3 week Marketplace wait and the global-client-plus-review path, but nothing states the roughly 1-hour time for the internal-use case.
